title: Two ropes, one crate
hook: Two ropes pull one crate, 3 N east and 4 N north. What is the total pull?

knows: forces have a size and a direction
the newton as a unit of force
doesNotKnow: that forces add as vectors, tip to tail
that the total depends on the angle between the forces

misconception: Forces simply add as numbers: 3 N + 4 N = 7 N whatever their directions.
objective: The learner can explain that forces add as arrows, so 3 N east and 4 N north make 5 N at an angle; 7 N happens only when both point the same way.

claims.text: Pulls of 3 N east and 4 N north have the same effect as a single 5 N force pointing 53° north of east.
claims.source: Vector sum (3, 4) N: magnitude sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5.000 N, direction atan(4/3) = 53.13 degrees. Re-computed in artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs.

claims.text: The net force on an object is the vector sum of the forces on it: arrows added tip to tail, in either order. The stage notes 'Order swapped: same single force.' when the order is swapped.
claims.source: Newton's second law with forces as vectors; vector addition is commutative (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 2.1 Scalars and Vectors and section 5.1 Forces). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Vector addition is commutative; net force is the vector sum (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, 2.1 and 5.1). Stage computes the resultant tip from the sum only, so swapping order draws the same resultant, and shows 'Order swapped: same single force.' when swapped.

claims.text: With the 4 N pull at an angle θ from the 3 N pull, the single force is √(25 + 24 cos θ) N: 7 N when they point the same way, 5 N at 90°, 1 N when opposed.
claims.source: Law of cosines for the vector sum. Stage values in 15-degree steps: 7.0, 6.9, 6.8, 6.5, 6.1, 5.6, 5.0, 4.3, 3.6, 2.8, 2.1, 1.3, 1.0 N (check.mjs).

claims.text: Model: seen from above on frictionless ice, so the two pulls are the only forces along the surface.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Top view, on ice') and in the reveal. Weight and the ice's support act vertically and cancel; friction is ignored.

recall.question: Two people pull a sled with 6 N each, at right angles to each other. Roughly how big is the total pull?
recall.why: At right angles the pulls form a right triangle: √(6² + 6²) ≈ 8.5 N. Only pulls in the same direction add to 12 N.
